## The End of an Era on Penn Avenue

For nearly a decade, the pink-and-white mural building on the corner of Penn
Avenue and South Beatty Street has been shorthand for East Liberty's tech
boom. Duolingo, the language-learning app that grew from a Carnegie Mellon
University research project into a publicly traded company worth billions,
has occupied that roughly 77,000-square-foot building at 5900 Penn Avenue
since 2016. That chapter is now ending. The company is relocating its
Pittsburgh headquarters to a larger space about half a mile away, and its
longtime home is already being marketed to new tenants.

## Where Duolingo Is Headed

Duolingo's new home is Liberty East, a mixed-use tower at 141 South St. Clair
Street, also in East Liberty and anchored on its ground floor by a Whole
Foods Market. The move isn't Duolingo's first connection to the building —
the company already leased around 38,000 square feet there starting in
November 2021. What's changing now is scale. Duolingo signed a 10-year lease
in March 2024 for roughly 140,000 to 150,000 square feet, nearly doubling its
local office footprint. The lease runs through June 2035, with a reported
cost of close to $400,000 per month. The full transition is expected to take
about a year to complete.

## What Happens to the Old Building

With Duolingo moving out, 5900 Penn Avenue is now on the market. Hanna
Commercial Real Estate is advertising the three-story property for sale or
lease, putting one of East Liberty's most recognizable addresses back into
play. For a neighborhood that has watched its retail and office corridors
stay in high demand, losing an anchor tenant like Duolingo raises real
questions about what comes next for the site — and whether another
high-profile company steps in, or the space gets reimagined entirely.

## A Pittsburgh Success Story, Still Growing

Duolingo was founded in 2011 by Carnegie Mellon University alumni Luis von
Ahn and Severin Hacker, and its Pittsburgh roots have remained central to its
identity even as it expanded into one of the most downloaded apps in the
world, serving hundreds of millions of users studying dozens of languages.
Keeping its headquarters in East Liberty rather than relocating to a larger
tech hub has long been treated locally as a point of pride — proof that a
homegrown Pittsburgh company could scale globally without leaving the city
that built it.

## What It Means for East Liberty

Nearly doubling office space in the same neighborhood signals something
different from a company quietly downsizing or leaving town — it's a bet
that East Liberty itself, not just Pittsburgh broadly, remains the right
place to grow. For local businesses near both the old and new addresses,
that continuity matters. A departure would have been a loss for the
neighborhood's daytime foot traffic; an expansion two blocks over keeps
that economic activity local, even if the exact building changes.

The Allegheny Chronicle will continue following how the vacated Penn Avenue
building gets reused, and what Duolingo's larger East Liberty footprint means
for the neighborhood going forward.
